description: Conducting a study in order to obtain permanent solutions for the issues arisen after construction of the Salinity barrier across the Matara Nilwala River
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-10-13 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Nilwala River is the main water source which supplies drinking water to several major cities including Matara City and the people residing in the Beliatta and Tangalle Divisional Secretariat Divisions of the Hambantota District. With the erosion of the bed level of the Nilwala River below sea level, salt water inflows to the pumping stations during dry seasons severely disrupting the supply of drinking water. As a solution to this issue, a structure of salinity barrier with 05 gates has been constructed during the period of 2018 and 2022. It has been revealed that due to the construction of the said structure of salinity barrier, the flow of water in the river is obstructed not only during flood situations but also during dry seasons, causing waterlogging of cultivated lands and hindering farming. Although studies have been conducted in this regard by the Hydrological and Disaster Management Division of the Irrigation Department and the Lanka Hydraulic Institute, it has not been possible to provide a sustainable solution for the issue so far. At a meeting held in this regard on 202509-08, under the chairmanship of the Secretary to the President, with the participation of all relevant parties, it has been decided to obtain a report from an independent institution representing qualified professionals in the engineering field. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation to have a study conducted for a sustainable solution to the problems that have arisen after the construction of the Matara Nilwala Salt Barrier from the Institute of Engineers Sri Lanka which is an institution in the type referred to above, was approved by the Cabinet.
